overview.summary: Lumen is a Cloudflare Worker that teaches software engineering to AI-assisted developers. It reviews AI chats, maps public GitHub repositories into architecture modules, explains commits, and helps start projects, all grounded in evidence from real files and lines.

modules.name: Web pages
modules.role: Serves static HTML, CSS, and JavaScript pages for chat review, repo mapping, commit explanation, and project kickoff.
modules.whyItExists: Provides the user interface so people can interact with Lumen without installing anything, keeping the frontend separate from the API logic.

modules.name: API routes
modules.role: Defines HTTP routes such as /api/chat/review and /api/repo/overview and dispatches requests to the correct handler.
modules.whyItExists: Separates request routing from business logic so each endpoint has a single responsibility and the server can be tested independently.

modules.name: Request logic
modules.role: Validates input, checks caches, enforces rate limits, and coordinates calls to GitHub and the LLM.
modules.whyItExists: Keeps validation, caching, and rate-limiting separate from route definitions so the same rules can be reused across endpoints.

modules.name: GitHub provider
modules.role: Fetches repository metadata, file trees, and commit data from the GitHub API.
modules.whyItExists: Encapsulates all communication with GitHub in one place so the rest of the app does not depend directly on an external HTTP API.

modules.name: LLM provider
modules.role: Calls NVIDIA NIM or Workers AI to generate explanations, prompt rewrites, and architecture maps.
modules.whyItExists: Isolates model interaction behind a single interface so the app can switch providers or add fallback behavior without changing handlers.

modules.name: Database
modules.role: Stores cached public-repo analyses and hashed IP rate-limit counters in Cloudflare D1.
modules.whyItExists: Persists only safe, public data so repeated repo analyses are faster while chats and ideas are never stored.

modules.name: Configuration
modules.role: Defines the Worker entry point, D1 binding, environment variables, and TypeScript build settings.
modules.whyItExists: Separates deployment and environment configuration from application code so the same code can run in development and production.

75e4848ca3807a42cfabfcaeac2106b525994cc6.title: Harden LLM timeouts and GitHub body-read errors, stronger chat review prompt, softer OAuth wording
75e4848ca3807a42cfabfcaeac2106b525994cc6.whatChanged: Extended the GitHub API fetch timeout from 10 seconds to 15 seconds in src/github.ts. Extended the LLM provider timeout from 25 seconds to 30 seconds in src/llm.ts and added a check that skips the second NIM attempt if more than half the timeout has already elapsed. Added a catch branch in src/index.ts that converts TimeoutError or AbortError into a 502 github_error response. Changed the chat review prompt version from chatReview-v2 to chatReview-v3 in src/prompts/chatReview.ts and added a rule that the strongest prompt is never listed as a problem, plus a filter in src/handlers.ts that drops any excerpt matching the overview's strongest prompt. Softened OAuth wording in public/concepts/concepts.json, changing "the safest way" to "the standard, safer way." Adjusted demo explain scores in scripts/make-demo.mjs from 4 to 6 for Lumen and from 3 to 5 for the Express blog API.
75e4848ca3807a42cfabfcaeac2106b525994cc6.whyItMatters: Long-running operations such as reading a large GitHub response body or generating a big repo overview can exceed short timeouts and surface as failures. The new timeout handling turns those delays into a clear, retryable 502 error instead of an unhandled exception. The prompt hardening prevents the review from incorrectly flagging the user's best prompt as a problem, making the coaching output more trustworthy. The OAuth wording change avoids overstating security guarantees.
75e4848ca3807a42cfabfcaeac2106b525994cc6.designReasoning: The system separates concerns by letting src/github.ts and src/llm.ts own their transport timeouts while src/index.ts owns the final error translation to the client. Skipping a redundant NIM retry when half the budget is consumed avoids wasting time on a slow-but-not-flaky provider. The chat review filter enforces a consistency invariant at the application layer: an excerpt identified as strongest cannot also appear as a finding.
75e4848ca3807a42cfabfcaeac2106b525994cc6.tradeoffs: Longer timeouts mean users wait longer before receiving an error when a provider is genuinely stuck. Skipping the second NIM attempt reduces total retry coverage in exchange for faster failure on slow providers. The stronger prompt filter may reduce the number of findings returned when the model's strongest excerpt overlaps with other candidate excerpts.
alternatives: Keep the original 10-second GitHub timeout and surface body-read errors as generic 500s.
Retry NIM unconditionally regardless of elapsed time.
Use a circuit breaker instead of a time-based skip for the second provider attempt.
Keep the chat review prompt unchanged and rely on post-processing to remove duplicate findings.

2594fa968ef212ef4b4ad8589a187dc159c76f27.title: Dedupe chat findings, add smoke test, CONTEXT.md, paper grain and card spotlight
2594fa968ef212ef4b4ad8589a187dc159c76f27.whatChanged: CLAUDE.md now tells developers to read and update CONTEXT.md. CONTEXT.md is new and records live URLs, deploy steps, AI model chain, trust rules, rate limits, known gaps, and Windows gotchas. base.css adds a fixed full-page SVG noise overlay behind main and footer so the cream background looks like paper grain. components.css makes each entry card a positioned overflow-hidden container with a radial-gradient spotlight that fades in on hover. home.js adds a pointermove listener to every .entry card that sets CSS variables --mx and --my to the pointer position inside the card. handlers.ts adds a seen Set in reviewChat that drops duplicate excerpts so each finding appears only once. scripts/smoke.mjs is new and checks pages return 200, health returns ok, unknown API routes return 400, short chat and non-GitHub repos are rejected, chat review returns non-duplicate items, and kickoff returns decisions and claudeMd.
2594fa968ef212ef4b4ad8589a187dc159c76f27.whyItMatters: CONTEXT.md keeps session state visible so work does not drift from SPEC.md. The smoke test catches broken deploys before users see them. Deduplication prevents the same chat finding from showing twice, which matches the trust rule that duplicate excerpts are dropped. Grain and spotlight improve visual polish without changing behavior.
2594fa968ef212ef4b4ad8589a187dc159c76f27.designReasoning: The commit follows CLAUDE.md's rule to build one step from SPEC.md section 12 per session and not add unplanned features. The trust model treats LLM output as untrusted, so reviewChat verifies excerpts are verbatim substrings of the chat and now removes duplicates. Free-plan limits (50 subrequests, 10 ms CPU, 100k requests/day) shape the API design, such as avoiding GitHub filesChanged subrequests.
2594fa968ef212ef4b4ad8589a187dc159c76f27.tradeoffs: Manual deploys mean no CI token yet, so the smoke test must be run by hand after each deploy. The radial spotlight uses pointermove on every card, which could add overhead on pages with many cards, but keeps the effect simple and dependency-free. The smoke test calls real AI endpoints, so it may be slow or consume rate-limit budget.
alternatives: Use CI/CD for automatic deploys instead of manual wrangler deploy
Use a CSS animation or canvas for grain instead of an inline SVG data URI
Use IntersectionObserver or a single mousemove listener instead of per-card pointermove
Skip AI calls in smoke test and only check static routes

cd98c42a8749f01886d5beb578a248605625a747.title: Fix text encoding corruption in repo.js and map.js
cd98c42a8749f01886d5beb578a248605625a747.whatChanged: Removed invisible byte-order-mark characters from the first line of public/js/map.js and public/js/pages/repo.js, and replaced corrupted arrow and middle-dot characters with correct UTF-8 characters in public/js/map.js line 82 and public/js/pages/repo.js lines 68 and 89.
cd98c42a8749f01886d5beb578a248605625a747.whyItMatters: Users saw garbled text such as â†’ instead of → and Â· instead of · in commit metadata and edge labels, and the byte-order-mark can break JavaScript module parsing.
cd98c42a8749f01886d5beb578a248605625a747.designReasoning: The files are frontend modules that render UI text; keeping source files as clean UTF-8 without a BOM and using correct arrow and dot characters ensures browsers parse the modules and display labels correctly.
cd98c42a8749f01886d5beb578a248605625a747.tradeoffs: None evident from the diff; the change only restores intended characters.
alternatives: Keep the corrupted characters and let users see garbled text
Use HTML entities such as → and · instead of literal UTF-8 characters

ed1896a5e57b4d40072d990e45b96efae0610fc5.title: Harden timeouts, add security headers, README and AI disclosure, regenerate examples
ed1896a5e57b4d40072d990e45b96efae0610fc5.whatChanged: Added security headers to public/_headers, expanded README with privacy, stack, libraries, fonts, local run steps, platform limits, and future work, added AI usage disclosure table to AI_USAGE.md, and regenerated public/demo/chat.json and public/demo/kickoff.json example data.
ed1896a5e57b4d40072d990e45b96efae0610fc5.whyItMatters: Security headers protect the browser from MIME sniffing, clickjacking, and overly broad referrer or content loading. The README and AI disclosure tell users how the app works, what models generated it, and what still needs human review. Regenerated examples keep demo data consistent with the current concept list and prompt tuning.
ed1896a5e57b4d40072d990e45b96efae0610fc5.designReasoning: Headers are served as static asset rules so every page gets protection without code changes. Documentation lives in markdown next to code so contributors see stack, limits, and AI provenance in one place. Example JSON is regenerated by a script so demo content matches the app’s current schema and concept ids.
ed1896a5e57b4d40072d990e45b96efae0610fc5.tradeoffs: Static headers apply to all routes and cannot be tuned per endpoint. README length grows to cover privacy and platform limits, which may overwhelm new readers. Regenerated examples replace hand-written text, so wording changes even when meaning stays similar.
alternatives: Set headers in the Worker code instead of _headers
Keep examples hand-written instead of script-generated
Omit AI disclosure and rely on commit history only

5f5fe0fd5443bb87ea9ec029e8af84a4b8d7f1e9.title: Frontend: design system, landing, chat review, repo map, kickoff, concept library, demo data
5f5fe0fd5443bb87ea9ec029e8af84a4b8d7f1e9.whatChanged: Added .claude/ to .gitignore so Claude-related files are not committed. Added public/chat.html, a new chat-review page with a textarea for pasting AI conversations, submit and example buttons, privacy text, and a results area. Added public/concepts/concepts.json, a 302-line JSON library of software concepts including client-server, api-route, http-methods, routing, database, schema, index, query, orm, migration, cache, and others, each with id, name, oneLine, explain, analogy, whenToUse, tradeoffs, and related fields.
5f5fe0fd5443bb87ea9ec029e8af84a4b8d7f1e9.whyItMatters: The chat page gives users a place to paste an AI conversation so Lumen can flag vague prompts and rewrite them. The concepts JSON provides a shared, machine-readable library of beginner software-engineering ideas that the app can reference when naming missing concepts. Ignoring .claude/ keeps local AI tooling out of version control.
5f5fe0fd5443bb87ea9ec029e8af84a4b8d7f1e9.designReasoning: The page separates structure (HTML), styling (linked CSS token/base/component files), and behavior (linked module script), following separation-of-concerns. The textarea uses maxlength and a live character counter to enforce input limits. Privacy text states chats are sent to an AI model then forgotten, addressing data handling. The concepts JSON uses flat objects with related arrays so concepts can be linked and looked up by id.
5f5fe0fd5443bb87ea9ec029e8af84a4b8d7f1e9.tradeoffs: Linking external Google Fonts improves typography but adds a third-party dependency and network round trips. Storing concepts as JSON is simple and language-independent but requires application code to load and search it; a database would be more scalable but heavier. A client-side textarea keeps input local until submit, but the privacy promise depends on server behavior not shown in this diff.
alternatives: Store concepts in a database instead of JSON
Use a frontend framework rather than static HTML
Keep .claude/ tracked instead of ignoring it
